title: Timing-Aware and Interpretable Self-Attention for Event-Based Wearable Task Transition Detection
abstract: arXiv:2610.27549v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Task transition detection aims to identify when a person shifts from one task to another, providing a foundation for continuous health monitoring and timely context-aware interventions. While statistical and deep feature representations have demonstrated strong classification performance, they often rely on aggregated or latent features that are difficult to interpret in behavioural terms. Event-based features provide a compact and interpretable alternative by encoding behavioural and physiological patterns as discrete tokens with explicit semantic meaning, making them well suited for behavioural analysis in health informatics. Self-attention offers a mechanism for modelling interactions among such tokens; however, conventional self-attention classifiers primarily rely on token order and do not explicitly incorporate timing or duration information. As a result, informative temporal cues in event representations may not be fully exploited

translated_title: 面向基于事件的可穿戴设备任务转换检测的时间感知可解释自注意力机制
translated_abstract: 任务转换检测旨在识别一个人何时从一项任务转换到另一项任务，为持续健康监测和及时的场景感知干预提供基础。尽管统计特征和深度特征表示已展现出强大的分类性能，但它们往往依赖于聚合特征或潜在特征，难以从行为角度进行解释。基于事件的特征通过将行为和生理模式编码为具有明确语义含义的离散标记，提供了一种紧凑且可解释的替代方案，使其非常适合健康信息学中的行为分析。自注意力为建模这些标记之间的交互提供了机制；然而，传统的自注意力分类器主要依赖标记的顺序，并未显式地纳入时间或持续时间信息。因此，事件表示中蕴含的有价值的时间线索可能无法被充分利用。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个时间感知且可解释的自注意力机制，通过在基于事件的可穿戴行为标记中显式建模时间与持续时间信息，改进了任务转换检测的性能与可解释性。
